# Humanizer

> See why your draft sounds like AI, then fix it. Humanizer quotes the words that sound machine-written, then rewrites the draft in one of five voices. It is a Markdown skill for coding agents: it names 55 AI writing patterns and reports a 0 to 100 AI-tell score. The skill and the optional zero-dependency Node CLI make no network call of their own; the rewrite runs on the agent's model. MIT license. Last updated 2026-11-17 for v0.8.4.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/Aboudjem/humanizer-skill/blob/main/README.md): what it does, install, a real before and after, FAQ, limits
- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/Aboudjem/humanizer-skill/blob/main/skills/humanizer/SKILL.md): the skill itself, the only file an install needs
- [Pattern deep dives](https://github.com/Aboudjem/humanizer-skill/blob/main/skills/humanizer/references/patterns.md): the 55 patterns with triggers, sources and before and after pairs
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Aboudjem/humanizer-skill/blob/main/AGENTS.md): how an agent works in this repo, with the test commands

## Install

- Claude Code: `claude plugin marketplace add Aboudjem/10x` then `claude plugin install humanizer@10x`
- Any agent the skills CLI supports, for all your projects: `npx skills add Aboudjem/humanizer-skill -g` (add `-a codex` or another agent code to pick one; drop `-g` for one project)
- [Per-editor paths](https://github.com/Aboudjem/humanizer-skill/blob/main/docs/editors.md): Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Zed, Kimi Code CLI, and the manual copy

## Use

- Rewrite: `/humanizer "your text"` or `/humanizer --file draft.md --voice technical`
- Detect only: `/humanizer "your text" --mode detect --score`
- Voices: `casual`, `professional`, `technical`, `warm`, `blunt`
- Score a file with the CLI: `node cli/index.js score draft.md`
- Gate a folder: `node cli/index.js scan docs --fail-above 40`
- Check a rewrite kept its facts: `node cli/index.js compare --before a.md --after b.md --check-facts`

## The 55 patterns

- P1 to P8, content: significance inflation, promotional language, AI vocabulary
- P9 to P18, language and style: negative parallelisms, dash overuse, structured-list syndrome
- P19 to P21, communication: chatbot artifacts, knowledge-cutoff disclaimers, sycophantic tone
- P22 to P30, filler and hedging: filler phrases, generic conclusions, uniform sentence length
- P31 to P43, emerging: elegant variation, placeholder text, markup leaks, infomercial hooks
- P44 to P55, craft and forensic: false agency, aphorism formulas, unicode obfuscation, hedge debris

## Limits

- The score reads four text signals. It is not a trained detector and it does not prove who wrote a text.
- The tool does not promise to pass any AI detector.
- The CLI metrics are built for English prose.
- The fact check finds lost numbers, dates, versions, URLs and acronyms. It does not check meaning.
